chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
A man who doubts after he has departed from his salat (prayer) — he said: So he said, he does not repeat, and there is nothing upon him.

However, the second report only included mention of one who prayed two rakʿahs and forgot two rakʿahs, and that occurs in the four-rakʿah prayers rather than salat al-ghadāh. Yet even if that is so, the ruling in that case also is like the ruling in salat al-ghadāh: that whenever he turns away to face away from the qiblah, repeating the salat (prayer) is incumbent upon him. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat (prayer) due to invalidity or deficiency
key_terms.اسْتِدْبَارِ الْقِبْلَةِ: turning one’s back away from the qiblah after prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer mentioned as having been performed or omitted
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.يَشُكُّ: to have doubt regarding the correctness or completeness of the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on doubting or realizing omitted rakʿahs after turning away from the qiblah following salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on doubt arising after completing salat (prayer), stating that if the person has already departed, he does not repeat it and nothing is due upon him. It then distinguishes a report about forgetting two rakʿahs in a four-rakʿah prayer, while affirming a similar ruling to salat al-ghadāh when one has turned away from the qiblah, in which case the salat (prayer) must be repeated.
